A1.justification: Both PDFs contain the same GRAPE research work. All 24 pages, including figures, tables, equations, and Appendices A–J, are readable and support a complete comparison.

before.justification: v3 reports original language-model training and validation losses on FineWeb-Edu in Figures 2–3 and downstream evaluation results on seven benchmarks in Tables 1–2.

after.justification: v5 retains the original FineWeb-Edu training and validation results and seven-benchmark evaluations in Figures 2–3 and Tables 1–2.

M1.justification: The multiplicative, additive, and path-integral GRAPE procedures, their components, and Appendix H pseudocode are unchanged. The model-size label correction does not establish an architectural change.

E1.justification: Both versions use FineWeb-Edu and the same ARC-E, ARC-C, HellaSwag, OBQA, PIQA, WinoGrande, and SciQ evaluations. Appendix G retains the same unevaluated 2D/3D extensions.

E2.justification: Comparator membership is identical within each experiment: RoPE, ALiBi, FoX, and the same GRAPE variants remain in Tables 1–2, including the corresponding comparisons with and without KV-shift.

E3.justification: The reported medium-model size changes from 350M in Section 6.1 and 355M in Figure 2 to 353M in both places. The stated layers, heads, hidden dimensions, training budget, and evaluation procedures remain unchanged; the PDFs do not establish model resizing or rerunning.

E4.justification: The contextual/noncontextual GRAPE, additive-gate, and KV-shift comparisons are unchanged. Neither the main text nor appendices add or revise robustness tests, sensitivity analyses, error analyses, or case studies.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run counts, random seeds, confidence intervals, error bars, or significance tests for the empirical results. Statistical reporting practices are unchanged.

E6.justification: All result entries, numerical scores, and rankings in Tables 1–2 are identical, as are the loss curves in Figures 2–3 and the reported qualitative findings. The amended model-size labels are experimental descriptions rather than changed performance results.

T1.justification: The mathematical definitions, assumptions, propositions, proofs, and derivations are unchanged throughout the main text and appendices, including the FoX equivalence, rank-2 exponential formulas, and spectral analysis.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction contributions, and conclusion retain the same claims about unifying multiplicative and additive positional encoding, recovering RoPE, ALiBi, and FoX, and supporting efficient extensions.

C2.justification: Section 6.2 retains the same performance and training-stability interpretations. The applicability, streaming, and spectral discussions in the appendices are also unchanged, with no new limitations or qualifications.

D1.justification: The experimental documentation reconciles the conflicting medium-model parameter counts by reporting 353M consistently. Other implementation details, hyperparameters, pseudocode, and the project/code access information remain unchanged.

R1.justification: The cited works and research positioning are unchanged, including Appendix A's related work, Appendix F's LieRE comparison, and Appendix J.4's PaTH discussion.

P1.justification: The first-page author list swaps the order of Yang Yuan and Kangping Xu, and the arXiv version/date stamp is updated. Two model-size labels are corrected; the remaining prose, section order, and appendix structure are unchanged.

P2.justification: Figure 2's caption changes its model-size label from 355M to 353M, and the author block has a small spacing adjustment accompanying the reordered names. Plot graphics, tables, and the overall page layout remain unchanged.

improvement.justification: v5 removes the inconsistency between the 350M model description in Section 6.1 and the 355M Figure 2 caption by using 353M consistently. This modestly improves experimental documentation clarity; the methods, theoretical content, and empirical evidence are unchanged.
